subject: Re: Finlytics — OpenAI-compat migration & competitive test plan
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Joel Bryant <joel@finlytics.ai>, Ava Patel <ava@finsuite.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Finlytics call recap + proposed OpenAI-compat tests

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment: 

Summary of discovery:
- Primary goal: move Finlytics' document summarization and insights pipeline off the hosted OpenAI endpoint to reduce per-token cost and gain predictable latency.
- Must preserve prompt/interface parity for current SDK calls (OpenAI-compatible API is a requirement).
- Competitive comparison youre running: OpenAI (baseline), Hyperscaler-managed endpoints (e.g., Bedrock), and self-hosted inference. Key criteria: latency (p50/p95), token cost, API compatibility, and model parity on our prompt set.

Redwood value props called out on the call:
- OpenAI-compatible public API surface (same request/response schema + SDK adapters) to reduce integration work.
- Automated prefix and KV caching that lowers per-token billing for repeated summaries.
- Routing and fallbacks (we can route to cheaper quantized variants in burst events to preserve availability).

Proposed evaluation plan (short):
1) Functional parity: run Finlytics' prompt suite (attached: finlytics_prompt_suite_v1.csv) against OpenAI and Redwood-openai-compat. Compare outputs for top-5 prompts.
2) Latency & cost microbench: 1k sample requests across representative prompt lengths (S/M/L). Capture p50/p95 latency and token issuance.
3) Quality diff: automated rouge/bleu-ish metrics (we'll add manual checks for 30 edge cases).
4) Integration check: provide an SDK swap guide (curl & node snippet below) and try a canary of 10k requests in your staging.

Quick SDK/curl examples to try immediately:
- curl
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions -H \"Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1.3-openai-compat\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":\"You are a helpful summarizer.\"},{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Summarize: <document>\"}]}'

- Node (openai-compatible adapter)
  const OpenAI = require('openai');
  const client = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, baseURL: 'https://api.redwood.example/v1' });
  await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'redwood-1.3-openai-compat', messages: [...] });

Attachments Im uploading to the Drive link below: finite prompt suite and the test plan (redwood_openai_compat_test_plan_v2.pdf).

Next steps we agreed on the call:
- Finlytics: share any additional edge-case prompts you rely on (Joel) by EOD Friday.
- Redwood: we'll provide a test harness and a small runbook to execute the microbench.
- Align on success criteria: <= 10% regression in summary quality, p95 latency <= current OpenAI baseline + 200ms, and total token spend <= 70% of current monthly spend for equivalent throughput.

Ill follow up with the test artifacts and a proposed schedule. Thanks — looking forward.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

Attachment: finlytics_prompt_suite_v1.csv (CSV, 42KB)
Attachment: redwood_openai_compat_test_plan_v2.pdf (PDF, 128KB)
From: Joel Bryant <joel@finlytics.ai>

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Finlytics call recap + proposed OpenAI-compat tests

Thanks Sergio — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side before we run anything:
1) For the OpenAI baseline, were using gpt-4o-mini currently for summarization (prompt engineering layer on top). Will Redwood provide model mapping guidance (which Redwood model most closely matches outputs)?
2) For tokens: our accounting today counts both prompt+completion; will your cost comparisons include the same calculation?
3) Security question: do you have SOC2 documents and an option for a Private VPC deploy if we decide to go on-prem for sensitive customers?

Well push our additional 20 edge-case prompts to you by Friday. Can your test harness produce side-by-side diffs that we can drop into our internal JIRA?

Joel
Head of Platform | Finlytics
joel@finlytics.ai

Joel — good questions. Short answers (and actions were taking):
1) Model mapping: Redwood-1.3-openai-compat is tuned for parity with instruction-following gpt-4o-mini on summarization workloads; well run a 50-prompt blind A/B to confirm match. Action: were including model mapping notes in the Drive test plan.
2) Cost calc: we will report prompt+completion token counts and use your current pricing model as the baseline. The Reduwood test harness outputs per-request token accounting in CSV so you can import it.
3) Security: yes — SOC 2 in our security folder; Private deployment is a supported path (we discussed VPC option during the call). Ive CCd Priya from Security & Private to loop on required documents and timelines.

Attached: redwood_openai_compat_test_plan_v2.pdf (Drive link) and Im attaching a quick-run script below you can drop into your staging: 

Quick-run Node script (pseudo):
- uses the finlytics_prompt_suite_v1.csv file (first column prompt_id, second column prompt_text)
- parallelize 50 concurrent requests, capture per-request latency and tokens
- output: finlytics_run_results_20260220.csv

We also created a side-by-side diff export format (CSV) that includes: prompt_id, openai_output, redwood_output, rouge_score, token_delta, latency_openai, latency_redwood. You can import that directly into JIRA as attachments.

Action items for Redwood team: 
- Marissa: own the test harness run and deliver initial A/B results by 2026-02-22.
- Rishi: compile model mapping doc + quantized variant suggestions (for cost tests).
- Priya: share SOC2 + Private deployment intake for Finlytics.

Will send the Drive links in a separate message to avoid hitting mail size limits.

—
Sergio
